central_finding_n4_phis: VERIFIED CORRECT IN CURRENT CODE. detect_loop_carried_coopmat (body.rs:932) iterates em.coopmat_binding_ids, filters to bindings with a pre-loop var_ids entry, sorts deterministically by BindingId, and pushes EACH carried binding with its OWN freshly-allocated phi_id -> Vec<(BindingId, Word)>. emit_for_range then builds pre_header_values[i] and latch_values[i] by mapping over `carried` in the SAME order, and step-10 inserts phis indexing pre_header_values[i]/latch_values[i] by the SAME i. The index i is the SINGLE key tying (bid_i, phi_id_i, pre_header_i, latch_i) together, so there is NO cross-contamination for any N: acc01's latch CANNOT be assigned to acc10's phi. Each acc_ij = coopmat_mul_add(...) rebinds ONLY its own binding's var_ids entry, so the post-body latch harvest reads each accumulator's own SSA id independently. The reverse-order InsertPoint::Begin insert (i = N-1..0) places all N phis at the header head in declaration order for ANY N, preserving SPIR-V 2.4 'phis first' (final header = [phi0..phiN-1, OpLoad i, OpULessThan, OpLoopMerge, OpBranchConditional]). The ONLY thing AT-1702 does not already cover is N>1 phis in ONE header (it has 1-phi-per-header across 2 headers) — but the Vec machinery is N-agnostic and the single-loop case differs only in count, not structure. The architect's 'no codegen change' claim is therefore PLAUSIBLY TRUE; AT-1733 (mandated below) LOCKS it as a pre-gate.

Do NOT silently mutate body.rs to make it pass.
warnings: WARNING (occupancy honesty gap, NON-blocking): §3 asserts 64 workgroups at M=N=256 is 'still ample for the GPU's SMs' but does NOT prove the per-workgroup arithmetic-intensity increase outweighs the occupancy drop. The RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell has ~188 SMs; 64 single-subgroup workgroups is FEWER workgroups than SMs and may UNDER-occupy — the RB kernel could be SLOWER, not faster, than M3.3b's 256-workgroup baseline. The architect must state this tradeoff EXPLICITLY in DESIGN/ROADMAP, not bury it in an edge-case bullet. MITIGATION: this is non-fatal because the acceptance gate is 'IMPROVED vs 5.04, reported HONESTLY, no asserted ratio' (AT-1730) — if RB is slower, the bench reports it and the honest winner (possibly M3.3b) stands. Larger M=N (e.g. 512/1024) would restore occupancy and is the natural follow-up if 256 under-occupies; the architect should note that the 256 measurement may understate RB's win for larger matmuls.

WARNING (barrier analyzer provides NO coverage for the reuse loads): coopmat_load-from-shared (typecheck.rs:2690) takes CoopMatLoadSource::Shared WITHOUT calling check_shared_read / analyze_shared_read_barrier. The cross-invocation RAW analyzer only fires on SCALAR SharedRead indexing, NOT on coopmat loads. Therefore the RB kernel's multi-offset reuse loads (A at offsets 0 and 256, B at offsets 0 and 16 — slots written by OTHER lanes) are NOT checked by the analyzer. This is NOT a new regression (M3.3b already loads coopmat-from-shared unchecked), but it means the reuse-index correctness rests ENTIRELY on the real-GPU bit-exact tests. AT-1731/1732 are therefore the ONLY proof of the A/B reuse math and MUST be non-symmetric and exercise multiple blocks AND multiple tiles per block — HN-7's M=N=64 (block grid 2x2, 2 tiles per block per axis) satisfies this. Do NOT weaken that fixture.

abreuse_index_assessment: CORRECT as specified. coopmat_load(shared, element_offset, stride) supports the offset+stride reuse (coopmat.rs:315 single-index Workgroup path). A shared block is (RB_M*16) rows x 16 cols (stride 16): i-th row-tile element_offset = i*16*16 = i*256 -> HN-1 '0 and 256', stride 16. CORRECT. B shared block is 16 rows x (RB_N*16) cols (stride RB_N*16=32): j-th col-tile element_offset = j*16, stride 32 -> HN-1 '0 and 16, stride 32'. CORRECT. Output c_base[i][j] = (block_row*RB_M*16 + i*16)*N + (block_col*RB_N*16 + j*16), stride N. Index recovery block_col=gid(0)/32, block_row=gid(1), lane=subgroup_invocation_id() mirrors M3.3b exactly. A TRANSPOSE/swap of A[i]<->B[j] or i<->j would be caught by the NON-symmetric AT-1731/1732 fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}, distinct per-tile) — confirmed the fixture is non-symmetric and multi-block.
register_occupancy_honesty_assessment: HONEST. §7 + edge_cases explicitly state: 2x2 (4 acc + ~4 transient = ~8 live coopmats) is safe; 4x4 (16 acc + 8 transient = 24) MAY spill and collapse throughput; SHIP 2x2, measure 2x4/4x4 best-effort, report the HONEST best (if 2x2 wins, 2x2 ships). No asserted 4x speedup; OQ-4 admits the win is bandwidth/issue amortization (~7-15%), not a guaranteed FLOP multiplier. Shared (2x2=2048B, 4x4=4096B) is correctly identified as NOT the cap, gated fail-closed by the existing SharedMemoryExceedsDeviceLimit preflight (context.rs:869). The hand-unroll expressibility boundary (OQ-1: no strategy-unroll, no coopmat array type) is honestly documented.
bit_exactness_assessment: PRESERVED. RB tiling changes ONLY loop/tiling structure, not the numeric op sequence: each acc_ij accumulates the SAME ordered coopmat_mul_add over the SAME K-blocks as a single-tile kernel for tile (i,j). Same tensor-core op + same accumulation order => bit-identical. No new rounding. AT-1620/1622 (single-tile) RETAINED as regression; AT-1731 (2x2 fixed K) + AT-1732 (K=32 vs K=48, varying OpPhi trip count) assert max_diff==0. The 4 unconditional top-level reassigns satisfy the AT-1708 conditional-reassign guard by construction (no if/else reassign) and the AT-1704 break/continue guard (none present).

summary: APPROVE with one BLOCKING pre-gate (AT-1733 first) and three non-blocking honesty warnings. The central claim — multiple loop-carried coopmat accumulators in ONE loop emit correct OpPhis with NO codegen change — is VERIFIED correct in the current body.rs: the parallel pre_header_values/latch_values/carried Vecs are indexed by a single i, eliminating cross-contamination for any N, and the reverse-order InsertPoint::Begin insert preserves 'phis first' for any N. AT-1702 covers the mechanism but not N>1-in-one-header, so AT-1733 is mandated as a hard pre-gate (Architect escalation, not Coder hack, if it fails). The A/B reuse index math (A offsets 0/256 stride16, B offsets 0/16 stride32, c_base recovery) is correct and transpose-catchable by the non-symmetric multi-block AT-1731/1732 — which are the ONLY correctness proof since the barrier RAW analyzer does not cover coopmat-from-shared loads. Register/occupancy honesty holds (ship 2x2, measure higher, report honest best, no asserted ratio). Bit-exactness preserved. Shared/grid bounds within limits, preflight gates fail-closed. THE SINGLE MOST DANGEROUS HOLE is the occupancy collapse: 64 single-subgroup workgroups at M=N=256 is FEWER than the GPU's ~188 SMs and may make the RB kernel SLOWER than the 256-workgroup M3.3b baseline; this is non-fatal ONLY because the acceptance gate is honest 'IMPROVED-or-reported', but the architect must state the occupancy-vs-arithmetic-intensity tradeoff explicitly and note that larger matmuls (M=N>=512) may be needed to realize RB's win.
